<!-- pr-reviewer: 453142b4963577dd3f9c8e8dd8a39bc21a529e9b -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- A script without `onProbeGuard` is refused by name, once per operation, with no silent plain-G01 default (engine.rs, new `Record::Guard` arm). That is the right call for a probing path.
- Arcs and rate-less feeds inside a probe path are refused with a WARN (`probe_rec::guard_of`). The new code has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic`.
- The `GUARD` record round-trips and refuses malformed lines (`parse_guard` rejects a missing `F` and a non-positive feed). `invert.rs` mirrors it like an absolute move. `viewer_map` and the moved-count in `posting.rs` count it.
- The Fanuc alarm (`G31` then `#3000` on any moving axis whose skip position differs from the target) and the Tormach `G38.3` then `#5070` test, `(MSG)` and `M2` are both sourced to public documentation. Provenance lines are updated, and the format is documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decisions file is in `docs/decisions/`, there is no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and the body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #174`. The Fanuc golden changes (G01 to G31 plus the alarm line) are what the body says they are.

**Local results (PR trial-merged with upstream/main 97661c8b, no conflicts)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --no-run` | builds |
| app probe_guard / probe_op / probe_pick / probe_reach | 5 / 11 / 9 / 5 passed |
| app fanuc_post / tormach_post / tormach_machines | 11 / 10 / 5 passed |
| app inverted_post / inverted_equivalence / inverted_axis_display | 15 / 2 / 4 passed |
| app posting / scripting / project_roundtrip | 17 / 18 / 69 passed |
| app conformance / per_op_files / post_not_judged | 6 / 5 / 9 passed |
| camcraft-post (all suites) | 48 passed (3 + 9 + 3 + 33), 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The PR changes no `build.rs`, `.github/` or scripts, and adds no dependencies.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. Order against #526: #526's tormach.cps change is the one line `if (spindleWait && sRpm > 0)` inside `startPreamble()` (around line 267). This PR adds a separate block after `onCircular()` (new lines 346-372). The hunks are disjoint, so there is no textual conflict. They also combine cleanly in behaviour: `onProbeGuard` calls `startPreamble()`, so with #526 a probe op will no longer get `S0 M3` ahead of its first guard block. I did not trial-merge #526 itself. It is fine to merge in either order.
2. Fanuc `onProbeGuard` calls `compRefuse(...)`. The Tormach hook does not, so any compensation check there depends on `startPreamble`/the other hooks. Check whether Tormach has an equivalent refusal for a protected move under G41/G42.
3. `guardO` on Tormach is a script-level counter. That is fine as long as the engine reloads the script per post run, which I believe it does since the tests show stable O-numbers.
4. Haas, Mazak and Siemens have no `onProbeGuard`, so their probe ops are refused by name once this merges. The body already flags this under #360.
5. The Tormach G38.3 / `#5070` / `M2` block is checked against documentation only, per the body. The contributor's PathPilot Hub comment covers it on the machine side.
6. `cnc.rs` (1006 lines), `mod.rs` (535) and `engine.rs` (462) were already over ~400 lines. This PR adds 13, 12 and 23 lines. That is flagged only, not blocking.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
